elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.2: "Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents ... and defend and save each of them harmless" — express defend obligation running to Customer and its Affiliates; no edit needed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.2: indemnity "from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees"; "AbbVie Indemnitees" expressly includes AbbVie's Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Inserted in 11.2: "(a) any Third Party Claim alleging that the Licensed Compounds or Licensed Products, or the intellectual property licensed to AbbVie hereunder, infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right of a Third Party" — the correct subject-matter analogue to Services/Deliverables in this development-and-option agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Inserted 11.2(b): "Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law". "Applicable Law" is the Agreement's defined term convention and is used consistently, so no dangling reference is created.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Inserted 11.2(c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of AbbVie's Confidential Information or data caused by Harpoon" — covers Vendor-caused data breach and is not limited to a narrow named data subset.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Inserted 11.2(d): "Harpoon's gross negligence or willful misconduct" — both limbs present.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.3: "The Indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice (an "Indemnification Claim Notice") of any Losses ..."; no edit made or needed.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.4.1: "at its option, the indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim by giving written notice to the Indemnified Party within [***]" — defence control is expressly allocated.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.4.4: "the Indemnified Party shall, and shall cause each indemnitee to, cooperate in the defense or prosecution thereof and shall furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Inserted after 11.1: "AbbVie's indemnification obligations under this Section 11.1 are limited to Third Party Claims to the extent arising from content or materials provided by AbbVie and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law." The "are limited to" formulation governs over the redacted trigger list, so the cap is operative rather than merely additive.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted 11.2(a) IP-infringement trigger satisfies the fallback IP limb.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification carve-out is added, and none is required; absence of the exclusion is more favourable to Customer, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination carve-out is inserted; its omission does not defeat the element and benefits Customer.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-specification carve-out is inserted; omission is permissible and Customer-favourable.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy ladder appears anywhere in the rendered 11.1–11.4 text; the insertion adds triggers only.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop is present; nothing in the inserted 11.2 list or retained Article 11 addresses refund on failure of alternative remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x-annual-fees super-cap is inserted; Harpoon's indemnity remains uncapped (11.5 limits only consequential damages). Deliberately omitted and Customer-favourable, but the fallback element is literally unmet.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the structural limbs (defend, Customer + Affiliates, notice, control of defence, cooperation) already existed in Articles 11.2–11.4 and were left untouched, and the two insertions supply the four missing Harpoon-side scope triggers plus the limit on AbbVie's own indemnity.

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met; the omitted super-cap is a Customer-favourable choice given the indemnity is presently uncapped.

Minimal: two additive sentences, no deletions, no survival tail, no expense/procedure/damages boilerplate, and no duplication of the existing notice, control and cooperation mechanics. The "without limiting the foregoing" framing preserves the redacted 11.2 triggers rather than overwriting them.

Intent preserved: no cross-reference is broken (Section 7.4's "Subject to Section 11.2" now has express IP support), and the 11.1 limitation is expressed as an operative cap that governs the redacted list rather than sitting alongside it in contradiction.

Residual drafting checks for the drafter (not defects on the face of the redline): confirm "Applicable Law", "Licensed Compounds" and "Licensed Products" are defined terms in Article 1, and be prepared for Harpoon to argue that the 11.1 limitation strips redacted allocations (e.g., AbbVie's Development/Commercialization conduct) — consider an "except as expressly set forth above" formulation if the redacted list is disclosed in negotiation.

Consider adding the conjunctive/disjunctive clarification in the 11.1 limitation ("arising from (i) content or materials provided by AbbVie or (ii) AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law") to avoid a reading that both limbs must be satisfied; as drafted the ambiguity runs in Customer's favour, so this is optional.
